name: Degrowth
summary: Degrowth holds that rich countries should plan a democratic, equitable reduction of energy and material throughput, because green growth has not delivered absolute decoupling. It pairs this with redistribution, shorter and shared work, decommodified public services and localised provision. It is explicitly not recession or austerity and not a demand for poor countries to shrink.
scope: The academic and activist degrowth movement of the 2000s to 2020s as set out by Hickel, the Degrowth.info editorial collective and Parrique's survey of the degrowth literature. It excludes steady-state economics and green-growth positions, and answers only where these sources state a position.

sources.title: The Political Economy of Degrowth
sources.author: Timothee Parrique, doctoral thesis 2019
sources.usedFor: Survey of 27 degrowth policy lists, the Barcelona declaration, population, migration, money and work.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Parrique's introduction lists moving beyond general-purpose money and wage-labour, while degrowth programmes also propose sovereign money and living wages.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Parrique's introduction places degrowth beyond wage-labour, yet Hickel's programme keeps wages through a living-wage job guarantee.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Barlow et al. say degrowth societies would treat animals with more care and respect rather than as commodities, and some advocates argue for animal liberation.

arms-reduction.rationale: Hickel lists arms among socially less necessary production degrowth would scale down.

basic-income.rationale: Parrique lists basic income as a degrowth strategy but reports degrowth writers such as Harribey and Laurut call it incompatible, and Hickel favours a job guarantee.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Parrique's thesis uses the hedonic treadmill to argue that ever more consumption adds little well-being, and Hickel wants wasteful production scaled down.

decide-locally.rationale: Parrique says degrowth aspires to decentralise governance to smaller grass-roots levels.

delink-world-market.rationale: Hickel endorses Samir Amin's delinking, refusing to subordinate national development policy to Northern capital, as an option for the South.

direct-votes.rationale: Parrique's survey of degrowth declarations records direct, participative democracy as a stated aim, though Latouche doubts direct democracy alone would choose degrowth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Hickel presents degrowth as part of a plan for a rapid transition to renewable energy, needed to stay within 1.5C and 2C carbon budgets.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Hickel's plan requires rapid transition to renewables and reversal of ecological breakdown, which expanding oil, gas and coal output contradicts.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Parrique's thesis uses nuclear power as an example of shifting environmental problems rather than solving them, and a degrowth demand list includes stopping nuclear power.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Policy lists surveyed by Parrique include a tax on international capital movements and financial transactions.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: Parrique's thesis describes gratuity, universal basic services free at point of purchase regardless of income, as a degrowth policy, matching Hickel's call for universal public services.

free-public-college.rationale: Hickel lists education among universal public goods degrowth would expand and decommodify; tuition-free college is not named specifically.

free-trade.rationale: Barlow et al. criticise unfettered globalisation and long supply chains, and Hickel rejects neoliberal globalisation's tenets as built on unequal exchange.

gm-crops.rationale: A degrowth policy list in Parrique's thesis proposes banning GMO research, and the thesis counts GMOs among non-convivial technologies.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Hickel attributes dangerous climate change to a particular economic system of perpetual expansion and cites the IPCC on carbon budgets.

job-guarantee.rationale: Hickel names a job guarantee with a living wage among degrowth's policies to prevent unemployment.

limit-growth.rationale: Hickel defines degrowth as a planned reduction of energy and resource throughput to bring the economy back into balance with the living world, and argues green-growth hopes lack grounding.

limit-population.rationale: The Barcelona degrowth declaration, quoted by Parrique, denounces top-down population control while welcoming falling birth rates, and Latouche calls restrictive population policy pointless.

local-production.rationale: Barlow et al. say degrowth proposes re-localising a significant amount of production on bioregional lines, shortening supply chains.

maximum-personal-income.rationale: Parrique's introduction lists a maximum income among degrowth policies and his thesis calls it one of the most popular degrowth demands.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Barlow et al. prioritise human and non-human well-being, and Parrique's care principle extends solidarity to non-humans.

open-borders.rationale: Parrique notes no degrowth consensus on migration; the Barcelona declaration backs a right to free migration but few others discuss it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Barlow et al. require a degrowth transformation to be democratic and list democratising society among five principles; Flipo's 'democracy source' says degrowth will be democratic or not at all.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Barlow et al. put justice and equality at the core of a degrowth transformation and say responses should prioritise the most vulnerable.

production-for-use.rationale: The degrowth New Roots principles, summarised by Barlow et al., say the economy must serve society and be organised around providing essential goods and services.

public-money-creation.rationale: Parrique's thesis proposes sovereign money created by a public body for social and ecological aims, and his glossary lists public money.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Hickel names living-wage policies among degrowth's tools to reduce inequality and protect livelihoods.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Parrique records that degrowth writers are divided or silent: some limit-immigration proposals exist while the Barcelona declaration supports free migration.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Hickel criticises structural adjustment for dismantling Southern developmentalist reforms and wants Southern governments freer to pursue human-centred economics.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Hickel calls for fair prices for Southern labour and resources, fairer terms of trade and finance, and more democratic representation in global governance.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Parrique's introduction states that degrowth is not a return to the past.

rich-first.rationale: Hickel rejects the argument that Northern excess consumption must continue because it is ultimately good for the South, comparing it to colonial-era justifications.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: A degrowth policy list in Parrique's thesis includes reforms against bank secrecy and tax havens.

simple-living.rationale: Parrique's introduction names voluntary simplicity as degrowth's individual level; the statement's stress on self-sufficiency is stronger than the sources.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Parrique's thesis reports debt cancellation as one of five degrowth-oriented actions proposed for the global South and lists a debt jubilee among degrowth policy proposals.

tax-inheritance.rationale: A degrowth policy list in Parrique's thesis includes a 100% inheritance tax, and he discusses inheritance tax revenue funding a universal allowance.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hickel lists progressive taxation to share income more fairly, and Parrique notes Hickel specifies an 80% income tax rate.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Hickel says degrowth expands universal public goods such as health to decommodify foundational needs, and the New Roots letter calls for decommodified health services.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Parrique's thesis argues for a right to be lazy and a post-work ethos, criticising work-centred society, and his introduction lists postwork.

worker-ownership.rationale: Parrique's introduction lists workers-directed cooperatives among degrowth's collective experiments and his thesis proposes worker ownership funds.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Parrique's survey of degrowth policy lists includes promoting democracy in the workplace through cooperatives, and New Roots calls for democratising society.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Hickel describes the North's net appropriation of Southern land, labour and resources through unequal exchange as a continuation of colonial relations.

missingStatements.text: Working hours should be limited by law so that work is shared among more people.
missingStatements.rationale: Hickel lists shortening the working week to prevent unemployment, and Parrique's thesis calls work time reduction the iconic degrowth reform.

notes: Parrique's thesis is one scholar's survey; answers resting on it alone are medium. Searched themes: economy, world, ecology, work, money, democracy, population and migration. Government, liberty and culture statements are mostly unaddressed.
